features.acceptance_check: The proposed process has its own version and differs visibly from the baseline.

features.acceptance_check: A failure to meet throughput remains visible even if savings look positive.

features.acceptance_check: A fractional time gain does not create an automatic staff reduction.

features.acceptance_check: Purchase cash flow does not count depreciation as a second cash cost.

features.acceptance_check: Costs are visible by year and by cost owner.

features.behavior: Show net annual cash saving, first-year cash flow, payback, life-cycle cost, cost per completed unit, and optional discounted value.
features.acceptance_check: A negative case shows no positive payback claim.

features.behavior: Limit the study to the agreed horizon. Show customer, site, and DP World retained benefit where required.
features.acceptance_check: A cost-plus benefit transferred to a customer is not counted as DP World cash saving.

features.behavior: Compare feasible options on throughput, quality, human work, cost, readiness, and evidence gaps. Explain trade-offs.
features.acceptance_check: There is no unexplained single score that can hide a failed constraint.

features.behavior: Show technical status, evidence basis, economic stress results, and deployment readiness separately.
features.acceptance_check: No percentage is labelled probability without a defined and supported method.

features.behavior: State the site/process, tasks assigned, people and equipment, demand met, cost, savings, payback, assumptions, gaps, and next action.
features.acceptance_check: The report names the exact process and configuration versions.

features.acceptance_check: Planned, in pilot, in service, paused, and retired assets remain distinct.

features.behavior: Enter or import throughput, good units, failures, interventions, active/charge/down time, human hours, and cost.

questions.question: Does the proposed flow define the correct product scope?
questions.proposed_default: Adopt the flow. Keep deployment and measured improvement in the same case.

questions.question: Does one shared workflow cover all technologies?
questions.proposed_default: Yes. Change the configuration, evidence, and deployment route by technology.

questions.question: Are Executive, Evaluations, and Deployments the correct three main views?
questions.proposed_default: Use these views. Put libraries under shared navigation.

questions.question: Must the mockup show only the tote PoC or also other use cases?
questions.proposed_default: Use the tote case as the main path. Add small, marked sample AMR, arm, and mixed-technology cases.

questions.question: Which outcome has priority when cost, capacity, quality, and readiness conflict?
questions.proposed_default: Meet hard requirements first. Show the feasible trade-offs. Do not set hidden weights.

questions.question: Which terms and languages must the product use?
questions.proposed_default: Use controlled English. Define task, work element, action, skill, capability, payback, and data status in a short glossary.

questions.question: What is the exact site and process for the first case?
questions.proposed_default: Confirm the automotive site name, empty tote types, sorting rule, source/destination, and approved SOP. Do not merge parts kitting into this PoC.

questions.question: What are the start/end points and upstream/downstream duties?
questions.proposed_default: Include tote presentation, placement, container exchange, blocked routes, and confirmation when they belong to the process.

questions.question: Which atomic process breakdown is authoritative?
questions.proposed_default: Use a site-reviewed breakdown. The mentioned process image was not available in this conversation; any drafted actions must stay illustrative.

questions.question: How much detail must an operator enter?
questions.proposed_default: Start with task and action. Offer work-element and motion detail when it changes fit or timing. Do not require every hierarchy level on every form.

questions.question: Which MTM or time-study methods are valid?
questions.proposed_default: Record the method and source. Support observed and standard times. Do not claim certified MTM without the required method and expertise.

questions.question: Which actions overlap or require the same person/tool?
questions.proposed_default: Record dependencies, shared resources, repeat counts, and parallel work. Do not sum overlapping action durations as elapsed cycle time.

questions.question: Which handoffs, supervision, retries, and recovery duties remain with people?
questions.proposed_default: Create explicit work records for each duty. Confirm their frequency and active time.

questions.question: Is the 5,000-tote example per person, team, shift, or day?
questions.proposed_default: Treat all numbers in the latest request as examples until their units and time windows are confirmed.

questions.question: Which engineering model is available and how does it derive staff?
questions.proposed_default: Map the required cells/fields manually first. Reconcile its assumptions with observed work.

questions.question: Which layout, scan, photo, and video files exist for the actual site?
questions.proposed_default: Store the files and manually map distances and clearances. Keep automatic CAD conversion as a future adapter.

questions.question: Which order, SKU, inventory, and event history can the site provide?
questions.proposed_default: Use a defined representative period and peak periods. Record missing coverage.

questions.question: Which workforce calendar and fully loaded cost basis apply?
questions.proposed_default: Use anonymous roles, shift coverage, productive hours, and current site rates. Separate annual headcount from people per shift.

questions.question: What restrictions apply to video, employee data, and cloud storage?
questions.proposed_default: Record permitted sources, processing location, access, and retention. Use synthetic media in the mockup.

questions.question: Who owns the technology library and approves each source?
questions.proposed_default: DP World owns the record structure. A named owner reviews supplier claims and trial evidence.

questions.question: Which AGIBOT model, gripper, sensors, SDK, and control access are available?
questions.proposed_default: Keep model and configuration unconfirmed. Do not infer a deployable stack from the vendor name.

questions.question: Which configuration combinations are supported?
questions.proposed_default: Compare only compatible hardware, tools, sensors, software, and interfaces. Mark unverified combinations unknown.

questions.question: Which specification limits include operating conditions and test methods?
questions.proposed_default: Capture the conditions for payload, reach, grip, speed, battery, sensing, and safety-related limits.

questions.question: Which prices and service terms can be used?
questions.proposed_default: Use dated quotes with inclusions. Keep the EUR100,000 robot price as an example until confirmed.

questions.question: Which solutions require configuration, custom control work, or model training?
questions.proposed_default: Ask the OEM/AWS to specify the route for each configuration. Do not assume training from scratch.

questions.question: When can supplier data support an initial process estimate?
questions.proposed_default: Permit labelled screening assumptions. Agree the evidence needed before a pilot recommendation.

questions.question: Is the first physics simulation required, and what question must it resolve?
questions.proposed_default: Keep this open. Compare a supplier benchmark, a bench trial, and a physics study against the missing task evidence.

questions.question: When can a task result be reused at another process or site?
questions.proposed_default: Define an operating envelope for object, pose, layout, tool, software, and conditions. Check differences before reuse.

questions.question: Which outputs must a simulation or benchmark provide?
questions.proposed_default: Return task times and ranges, first-pass success, retries, failures, recovery, conditions, sample count, and versioned inputs.

questions.question: What trial sample and error measure are sufficient?
questions.proposed_default: Define the success event and variability first. Agree the test design before setting a confidence claim.

questions.question: What bounds should the search use for fleet sizes and mixed technologies?
questions.proposed_default: Expose minimum/maximum counts, compatible task bundles, and shift options. Report the options actually evaluated.

questions.question: Which peak, downtime, and demand-growth cases must pass?
questions.proposed_default: Include agreed normal, peak, failure, and growth cases. Keep them as scenarios unless probabilities are supported.

questions.question: How do robots share chargers, buffers, routes, and human support?
questions.proposed_default: Use an explicit schedule/resource model. A simple average availability factor is a screening limit.

questions.question: Can the tool propose layout or process changes?
questions.proposed_default: Yes, as a separate option with its own time, cost, constraints, and evidence. Keep the current method visible.

questions.question: What part of freed time can create cash savings or avoided hires?
questions.proposed_default: Require a shift/staffing plan. Show redeployed capacity separately. Do not multiply task-count coverage by salary.

questions.question: Does EUR75,000 mean annual fully loaded cost per person?
questions.proposed_default: Keep it as a user example. Confirm currency, benefits, overtime, agency cost, paid hours, and effective date.

questions.question: Which purchase, lease, or RaaS offers should be compared?
questions.proposed_default: Model upfront and recurring costs by line item. Prevent duplicate service and maintenance costs.

questions.question: Who pays the costs and who retains the benefit under the site contract?
questions.proposed_default: Show DP World and customer views where needed. Allocate recovery cost separately from the share of labour benefit retained.

questions.question: What contract term, ramp-up, horizon, and exit costs apply?
questions.proposed_default: Use an agreed finite cash-flow period. Test contract end, redeployment, and residual value explicitly.

questions.question: Which payback limit, discount rate, FX date, and financial definitions apply?
questions.proposed_default: Call a two-year recovery of investment payback. Define ROI separately. Leave rates unknown until agreed.

questions.question: Which quality, capacity, safety, or service gains can be monetised?
questions.proposed_default: Show the metric first. Add money only with an agreed method and no double counting. Separate robot value from added platform value.

questions.question: What event would a confidence percentage describe?
questions.proposed_default: Define task success, process SLA success, and positive business case as separate questions with stated conditions and time windows.

questions.question: Can the evidence support a probability, or only a quality rating?
questions.proposed_default: Show evidence status and scenario ranges first. Leave probability unavailable until the method is supported and checked.

questions.question: How should evidence age, missing conditions, and site differences affect the result?
questions.proposed_default: Show specific gaps and transfer limits. Do not hide them inside a weighted score.

questions.question: What evidence permits advance to a benchmark, pilot, or scale-up?
questions.proposed_default: Agree a separate evidence requirement for each decision. A strong financial case alone does not prove readiness.

questions.question: Who is the accountable integrator from recommendation to site operation?
questions.proposed_default: Name one owner for the full delivery path. Split supplier/AWS/DP World duties in the plan.

questions.question: What model/policy or OEM software will run on the humanoid?
questions.proposed_default: Ask AWS/OEM to name the supported stack, access, rights, hardware limits, and fallback route.

questions.question: Which datasets, labels, simulation assets, and training runs are required?
questions.proposed_default: Define them only after choosing the execution route. Link each item to a task, failure case, and test.

questions.question: What must pass before loading hardware and starting a site pilot?
questions.proposed_default: Specify bench tests, interface tests, operating limits, site readiness, safe stop/recovery, and the accountable site decision.

questions.question: Who packages, loads, checks, monitors, and rolls back a release?
questions.proposed_default: Assign these duties explicitly. Preserve the previous release and its compatible configuration.

questions.question: What pilot duration, stop rules, and acceptance measures apply?
questions.proposed_default: Agree output, quality, intervention, downtime, human work, cost, and safety-related stop conditions before the trial.

questions.question: Which WMS/WES/PLC/fleet interfaces are required?
questions.proposed_default: Define dispatch, acknowledgement, exception, ownership, retry, and event contracts. Keep the platform separate from real-time machine control.

questions.question: What counts as a deployed asset and where is its status authoritative?
questions.proposed_default: Separate planned, in pilot, in service, paused, and retired. Record site, process, serial/configuration, and release.

questions.question: Which telemetry and actual cost data will be available?
questions.proposed_default: Start with manual/CSV input. Define denominators, timestamps, and downtime reasons before connecting live feeds.

questions.question: How will field data change task evidence and future recommendations?
questions.proposed_default: Review new evidence, record its operating envelope, update versions, and mark affected results out of date.

questions.question: When can a pilot scale to more robots or another site?
questions.proposed_default: Use observed performance and a fresh local gap check. Do not copy a site approval automatically.

questions.question: Where must version 2 store cases?
questions.proposed_default: Use local persistence plus complete validated export/import first. Add a shared backend only if collaboration needs it.

questions.question: Which roles need different views or edit rights?
questions.proposed_default: Show Executive, Engineer, Site, and Delivery views as demo roles. Treat real login and shared access as a separate implementation choice.

questions.question: Which integrations must be working in the mockup?
questions.proposed_default: Implement local records, rules, scenario maths, reports, and observed-data entry. Show CAD, physics, training, and hardware transfer as explicit placeholders.

sources: Defines the current design request. Deployment is part of the target platform. Validate the flow before the rebuild.
Rohit links process and MTM data to partial process augmentation. The input list includes process flows, layout, demand, inventory, and SKU data.
AWS workshop: business case and inputs

The discussion covers contract length, economics, comparisons, training, deployment, layout files, site data, workforce, resources, battery time, constraints, SLAs, and traffic. Several speakers share transcript blocks.

The discussion separates reusable performance metrics from full physics work for each scenario. The need for the first physics simulation remains disputed. Some speech is duplicated under different names.
Rohit and Radoy describe work split between people and machines, capability records, a business case, deployment, and later improvement.

The team distinguishes different configurations from repeated runs. The first prototype excludes physical deployment. The later internal discussion identifies a missing role that connects the product goal to technical work.

Useful hierarchy, task records, skills, measurable capability needs, source records, and exception links. The specification describes intended rules; code and sample data do not prove field capability.
Editable process revisions, structural checks, source links, and historical decisions. The current implementation uses session state.
A task that passes the checks receives its full fteCount as estimatedAutomatableFte. Building-block coverage is separate. This cannot establish a partial labour saving.
Useful lifecycle stages, hard physical checks, fleet sizing fields, charging, recovery cost, retained benefit, review records, and an export brief. The calculation is a planning estimate.
Profiler has three mode buttons and eight tabs. AMR has a separate ten-stage journey. The saved image was inspected. It does not establish the current runtime state.
A client and normalizers exist for the twin API. They are not evidence of a working robot training or physical deployment service. The backend was not run for this design review.
The current model uses process-level scores, fixed residual-work assumptions, and a score called confidence that includes economics. Version 2 needs a different calculation contract.
